note: Config Log subscribes to core config CRUD events and writes each change to up to three destinations: the custom DB table config_log (destination key 'custom'), watchdog/dblog via the default PSR logger (key 'default'), and email (key 'mail'). All behaviour is driven by the single config object config_log.settings (destinations, ignore list + negate, logs_to_keep retention, redact_sensitive_config_values, context lines). There is no plugin type and no Drush command; extension is by adding another EventSubscriber. Medium/hard cases are grounded in that real config object: introspection reads back retention/ignore values, execution flips real settings keys (enable the 'default' destination, add a user.* ignore pattern) verified against the live config.

evals.prompt: Using the config_log (Configuration Log) Drupal module, where can it send configuration changes? Name its destinations and where the changes are stored by default.
evals.expected_output: It has three destinations selectable on its settings form: the custom database table config_log (key 'custom', the default), the default logging system / watchdog-dblog via the PSR logger (key 'default'), and email/mail notification (key 'mail'). They are stored under config_log.settings:log_destination.

evals.prompt: Does the config_log module store secrets like passwords and API keys when it logs configuration, and how is that controlled?
evals.expected_output: By default it redacts likely-sensitive leaf values (passwords, secrets, tokens, API keys, client secrets, SMTP passwords) to [redacted] before storing/logging, redacting only the matching leaf. It is controlled by the boolean setting config_log.settings:redact_sensitive_config_values (default true).

evals.prompt: With config_log, how do I stop the config_log database table from growing forever, and what setting controls how many entries are kept?
evals.expected_output: Set config_log.settings:logs_to_keep to a positive number (0 = keep all; the UI offers 100/1k/10k/100k/1M). config_log_cron() then prunes the config_log table down to that many most-recent rows in batches on each cron run.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site config_log is already configured. Inspect the live config_log settings and state how many log entries it is set to retain in the custom config_log table.
evals.expected_output: config_log.settings:logs_to_keep is 1000 (destinations custom + default are active).

evals.prompt: config_log on this site is set to skip logging changes to some configuration. Inspect the live config_log settings and state which configuration name pattern is being ignored.
evals.expected_output: config_log.settings:log_ignored_config contains the pattern system.* (with log_ignored_config_negate false, so matches are skipped rather than the only thing logged).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site config_log currently logs only to its custom database table. Configure config_log so that configuration changes are ALSO written to Drupal's default logging system (watchdog/dblog). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: In config_log.settings:log_destination the 'default' key is present and truthy (e.g. {custom: custom, default: default}), so the ConfigLogPsrSubscriber logs to logger.channel.default.

evals.prompt: Configure the config_log module on this site so that it does NOT log any changes to configuration objects whose name starts with 'user.' (for example user.settings, user.role.*). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: config_log.settings:log_ignored_config contains the pattern user.* and log_ignored_config_negate is false, so any config name matching user.* is skipped by isIgnored().
